rules.title: Component with an intent-filter has no android:exported
rules.fix: Android 12+: activities, services and receivers that use intent filters must declare android:exported, or the app can't be installed on Android 12 or higher. Set true for the LAUNCHER activity; in most other cases false.

rules.title: Foreground services without a foregroundServiceType
rules.fix: Apps targeting Android 14 must give foreground services a type (camera, location, mediaPlayback, dataSync and others), plus the matching permission. If a service isn't a foreground service, ignore this.

rules.title: Release build is signed with the debug key
rules.fix: Google's signing docs: the debug certificate is insecure by design and most app stores, including Google Play, do not accept apps signed with it. Create a release keystore and point the release build type at it.

rules.title: iOS app icon is missing or not 1024x1024
rules.fix: Apple's Human Interface Guidelines specify a 1024x1024 px square app icon for iOS (layered, via Icon Composer in Xcode 26, or an AppIcon asset). Add a 1024x1024 image to the icon set. Apple's upload validation of this was not confirmed.

rules.title: No launch screen configured
rules.fix: Apple documents UILaunchScreen (no storyboard) and UILaunchStoryboardName as the keys that define the launch screen. What happens without one is not stated on those pages.

rules.title: Deployment target below the App Store minimum
rules.fix: Since 9 September 2026, iOS and iPadOS apps uploaded to App Store Connect must target iOS 13 or later. Raise IPHONEOS_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET (or the Podfile platform line). Extension and test targets may be listed too.

rules.title: CI builds with an Xcode older than the upload minimum
rules.fix: Since 28 April 2026, apps uploaded to App Store Connect must be built with Xcode 26 or later using the iOS 26 SDK. Update the Xcode version your CI uses.

rules.title: Push notification code without the aps-environment entitlement
rules.fix: Enable the Push Notifications capability in Xcode; that adds the aps-environment entitlement (Xcode sets development or production from the provisioning profile). If your signing is configured outside the repo, ignore this.

rules.title: Background mode without matching code
rules.fix: Guideline 2.5.4: multitasking apps may only use background services for their intended purposes (VoIP, audio playback, location, task completion, local notifications and so on). Remove modes you don't use.

rules.title: Payment SDK without an in-app purchase library
rules.fix: If the app sells digital content or features (subscriptions, in-game currency, premium access, unlocking functionality), Apple 3.1.1 requires in-app purchase and Google Play's Payments policy requires Play Billing. Physical goods and real-world services are different; if that is all you sell, ignore this.

rules.title: App Store text is over its length limit
rules.fix: App Store Connect limits: name 2 to 30 characters, subtitle 30, promotional text 170, description 4,000, keywords 100 bytes.

rules.title: Play listing text is over its length limit
rules.fix: Google Play limits: app name 30 characters, short description 80, full description 4,000.

rules.title: App Store screenshots have an unaccepted size or count
rules.fix: App Store Connect needs at least one and at most 10 screenshots per device size, in .jpeg, .jpg or .png, at one of the accepted pixel sizes (listed on the source page; framed or resized images fail).

rules.title: Play phone screenshot count is outside 2 to 8
rules.fix: Google Play wants two to eight phone screenshots on the main store listing.

rules.title: No privacy policy link found
rules.fix: Apple requires a Privacy Policy URL for iOS and macOS apps, and Google requires a valid privacy policy in both the store listing and inside the app. This check only looks in app code, config and store metadata files; the URL you enter in the store consoles is not visible here.

rules.title: User-generated content without report/block moderation
rules.fix: Apple 1.2 requires a way to filter objectionable content, a mechanism to report it, the ability to block abusive users, and published contact information. Google Play requires terms users accept, an in-app system to report and block, and ongoing moderation.
